subject: NordiceBank — follow-up: cross-border routing & deployment preference
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.h@redwood.com>
To: Lars Johansen <lars.j@nordicebank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.c@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.p@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Feb 2027 14:12:00 +0100
Subject: NordiceBank — follow-up: cross-border routing & deployment preference

Hi Lars — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on residency and deployment options: 

Summary of what I heard:
- Primary requirement: all production customer data for EU customers must remain within EU jurisdiction and be processed in an EU data region.
- Cross-border access: small set of analytics and billing queries may be allowed from the US under signed contract language & DPA, but latency-sensitive inference for EU customers should NOT egress to non-EU regions.
- Preferred modes: you asked for a Hosted API evaluation first (to move quickly), but compliance prefers Dedicated or Private VPC if Hosted cannot guarantee EU-only routing and private connectivity.

Options I propose we validate next: 
1) Hosted EU-only: our hosted API from EU region with data residency commitments + contract language. Fastest path to pilot; we will confirm routing & controls.
2) Dedicated EU capacity: reserved GPU pool in our EU region (SLA + isolation). Good middle ground for predictable throughput.
3) Private VPC (customer-managed VPC peering / on-prem): for strict residency + network controls — takes longer to set up (network, KMS, audit hooks).

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Lars: can you confirm whether any workloads require access from APAC or non-EU offices (e.g., Helsinki devs are fine, but Tokyo/NY teams may need occasional access)?
- NordiceBank: please share the list of systems that will call the API (to scope IP allowlists / peering).
- Redwood: we will send SOC2 evidence, a draft DPIA template, and a short model-routing diagram (attached) — please review and flag gaps.

Ill coordinate with Ben on a detailed timeline for Dedicated & Private setup and propose an initial pilot checklist you can share with procurement and security.

Thanks — Mina
Mina Haddad
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mina.h@redwood.com | +44 20 7946 0xxx

Attachments referenced: Redwood_Security_Overview_SOC2_v2.pdf; DPIA_template_NordiceBank.xlsx; network-topology-vpc-sketch.png
From: Lars Johansen <lars.j@nordicebank.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.h@redwood.com>
Cc: Sindre Berg <sindre.berg@nordicebank.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Feb 2027 15:02:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: NordiceBank — follow-up: cross-border routing & deployment preference

Mina — thanks for the tidy recap. Confirming a few points from our side:

1) Data residency: EU-only for production inference and persisted logs. Development/test data can live outside EU but must be clearly separated.
2) Consumers: primarily our customer-facing services hosted in our Frankfurt VPC. A small analytics team in London will query coarse usage metrics — they do NOT need token-level access.
3) APAC: not in scope for this pilot. We will evaluate APAC later but want EU solved first.

On deployment preference: security favors Dedicated or Private VPC. Procurement wants to understand time-to-value for Hosted (if we can get contractual assurance + technical controls to keep data in EU). Can you put together a short matrix (risk vs speed) so we can present to CISO and procurement?

Also: please send the DPIA template ASAP — our privacy lead will start mapping controls.

-Lars
Lars Johansen
Head of Data Platforms, NordiceBank
lars.j@nordicebank.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.c@redwood.com>
To: Lars Johansen <lars.j@nordicebank.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.h@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.p@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Feb 2027 16:05:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: NordiceBank — follow-up: cross-border routing & deployment preference

Lars / team — quick note from the infra side with the matrix you requested. Attached is a one-page risk vs speed matrix and a proposed minimal pilot plan. High level: 

- Hosted EU-only (fastest): Pros — hours to days, no infra changes; Cons — need contract addendum + routing verification and strict logging controls. Recommended if procurement accepts contractual guarantees and we can do a log/route PR review.
- Dedicated EU capacity (balanced): Pros — reserved capacity, stronger isolation, SLA options; Cons — provisioning ~2–3 weeks for initial pool and baseline throughput testing.
- Private VPC/on-prem (most controlled): Pros — full network control, KMS/HSM integration; Cons — 4–8 weeks setup, network ops involvement.

Pilot proposal (minimal): 
- Phase A (2 weeks): Hosted EU-only pilot with strict EU routing + transparent token-level logging (redacted) for compliance review.
- Phase B (4–6 weeks if required): move to Dedicated EU pool with peering test; or Private VPC onboarding if procurement/security require it.

We will include specific checklist items for procurement + security (DPA language snippets, IP ranges, peering docs). Mina will follow up with timeline and a short MAB (mutual action plan) you can share.

Ben Carter
Sr Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.c@redwood.com

Attachment: RB-EU-routing-risk-speed-matrix.pdf
From: Sindre Berg <sindre.berg@nordicebank.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.c@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.h@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Feb 2027 16:38:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: NordiceBank — follow-up: cross-border routing & deployment preference

Thanks Ben — that matrix looks useful. A couple of clarifications from security:

- For the Hosted option: what mechanisms do you use to guarantee EU-only processing? Is there an IP-level routing table we can review, or an assurance statement?
- For logs: our privacy team requires proof that token-level logs are never stored outside EU in the pilot; redaction is fine if you can provide an audit trail.

If you can share the routing verification doc and the DPIA template, well aim to review by next Tuesday (9 Feb) and get back with a recommendation for CISO.

Cheers — Sindre
Sindre Berg
Information Security Manager, NordiceBank
From: Mina Haddad <mina.h@redwood.com>

Sindre / Lars — thanks, noted. Next immediate deliverables from Redwood (Ill send links and files by EOD):
- Hosted EU routing verification doc (step-by-step config and IP ranges) — for your security team review.
- DPIA_template_NordiceBank.xlsx (editable) — privacy can map controls directly.

If procurement/CISO prefers Dedicated or Private after review, Ben will give a provisioning timeline and well schedule a technical workshop (30–60m).

I'll also open a shared Drive folder and drop the checklist + a lightweight SOW draft for procurement. Expect links shortly.

Regards — Mina
